question: How many people live within 1 km from a railway in Bangladesh
submittedPrompt:
How many people live within 1 km from a railway in Bangladesh

Task conventions: Use the frozen Bangladesh WorldPop 2018 bgd_pd_2018_1km_UNadj raster. Its verified units are people/km², NOT people per cell; preserve its original band, grid and missing mask. Convert density to population per cell using each original full WGS84 ellipsoidal meridian/parallel cell area in km², not a constant nominal 1 km². Use all original features in the supplied Bangladesh railway line inventory; no live railway substitutions, attribute exclusions or duplicated population from overlapping corridors. Define proximity by shortest planar distance from each original raster cell centre to the original railway geometries transformed into EPSG:32646 (UTM zone 46N), with original straight segments. A cell qualifies at distance <= 1000 metres. This is an explicit local projected cell-centre approximation, not travel distance or exact ellipsoidal distance. Projection distortion and unresolved within-cell population location remain limitations. The corridor includes the full cell when its centre qualifies, counting each cell once. Zero density is valid; missing/nonfinite cells remain unknown. Total and selected population are sums of density times physical cell area over valid cells; percentage is 100 times selected/total. Publish a selected-population raster (derived people per cell when qualifying, zero in other valid cells, original mask) and a distance raster in metres on that same original grid. The historical population and later railway snapshot do not prove contemporaneous access or census accuracy.



Compute the percentage and publish both inspectable rasters. A map is optional. End with a fenced JSON object: {count: qualifying cell count, unknown_count: original masked/nonfinite cell count, coverage_note, selection:{collectionId,itemId,assetKey}, distance:{collectionId,itemId,assetKey}, metrics:{selected_people:number,total_people:number,percentage:number}}. Label selected population as people per cell and distance as metres. Report the historical year and coverage limitations. Do not round machine-readable metrics to integers.

Delivery format: submit the structured answer through the final-result tool and finish with a matching concise response. [Product-specific tool arguments omitted.]

finalAnswer:
About 20.74 million people, or 12.777704565401805% of the valid 2018 WorldPop population in this Bangladesh raster, live within 1 km of the supplied railway lines across 8,123 qualifying cells. I published the selected-population raster in people per cell and the distance raster in metres. This uses historical 2018 population with a later 2025 railway snapshot, and 226,139 masked cells remain unknown.

investigations.question: Does the full requested processor chain preserve the supplied WorldPop grid and mask while correctly converting density to people per cell, selecting valid cells within 1000 metres of the supplied railways, and producing the requested Bangladesh-wide totals?

investigations.findings: The full Bangladesh trial preserved the supplied WorldPop grid exactly at 559×728 cells in EPSG:4326 with the same bounds, transform, and 226139 missing cells across the people-per-cell, distance, and selected-population rasters. The distance surface used projected-features with EPSG:32646 over all 2506 supplied railway features and produced metres on the original valid-cell mask. Map algebra kept zero as a valid outside value and did not create finite output where an input was missing. The derived people-per-cell raster summed to 162285835.78281653 people over 180813 valid cells, the selected-population raster summed to 20736404.647821426 people, and the qualifying 0/1 mask summed to 8123 qualifying valid cells with the same 226139 unknown cells.
limitations: This trial uses the requested local projected cell-centre approximation in EPSG:32646, so projection distortion and within-cell population location still limit interpretation.
